_comment: JTE's own layer on top of the weekly market pull. salary-data.json is
overwritten every Saturday by the refresh, so anything we know that the
raw numbers do not must live HERE or it gets wiped.
scripts/resolve-salary.mjs merges this over the raw pull.

floor.appliesTo: Full-time basic monthly salary, Singapore, 5-day week
floor.short: Below about S$2,500 basic a month, a role gets much harder to fill locally.
floor.long: This is not a rule, it is what we see. You can hire below it, but expect to wait a lot longer and to lose people to the employer up the road. Everyone is comparing. For hands-on roles on a 5-day week, S$2,500 is roughly where the market starts now.
floor.exemptNote: The S$2,500 guide is about basic pay where the basic is the whole package. Plenty of hands-on roles run a lower basic with overtime and incentives on top, and there you judge the gross instead. Where we know both, we show both.

operative.label: Hands-on roles
operative.note: Hands-on roles do not really have a junior-to-senior ladder, but they do have two numbers that matter. The basic is what you commit to. The gross is what the person takes home once overtime, incentives and allowances land, and it is the number they compare against the employer up the road. Supervisor and team leader roles sit separately, because that is more responsibility rather than the same job for longer.

professional.label: Professional & executive roles
professional.note: Banded by experience, because that is how employers brief us.

engineering.note: Two different entry points here. ITE-level technical roles start around S$2,500 to S$2,750 basic. A local diploma engineering hire starts at S$3,000 and above, which is what the bands below show. Shift and site allowances sit on top for the hands-on roles.

floor.appliesTo: Basic monthly salary, Singapore production and operator roles
floor.short: In manufacturing the basic is only half the story. Aim for a gross around S$3,000.
floor.long: Production and operator pay runs a lower basic than most sectors, with overtime and incentives doing a lot of the work. Around S$1,800 basic is the practical minimum anyone will take. Start the basic at S$2,000 and you are in the normal range; S$2,200 to S$2,500 and you attract noticeably better production staff. But the number people actually judge is the gross, and around S$3,000 a month is what tends to win them. Fewer people want to chase overtime these days, so a package that only works with heavy OT is a harder sell.

manufacturing.note: Pay is only half of it here. How straightforward the scope is moves the number as much as the band does, and at the lower end of the basic range the pool is smaller and the search takes longer. Tell us the scope and we will tell you what it will actually take to fill.

engineering/Engineering Technician.basicNote: Entry sits around S$2,500, but S$2,750 basic is the mark to stay competitive for ITE-level technical roles, because employer-sponsored diploma schemes have pulled entry pay up to about there. Below S$2,500 you will struggle for quality candidates. Shift and other allowances sit on top of all of this.

logistics/Warehouse / Store.verifiedNote: JTE, Nov 2026. Below S$2,500 basic is not the norm any more.
logistics/Warehouse / Store.aboveNote: Above this you are into team leader or assistant supervisor, which is more responsibility rather than a wider job scope. We list that separately.

logistics/Driver.basicNote: Judge a driver package on the gross, not the basic. A low basic with strong incentives is normal here, and how demanding the run is moves the basic as much as experience does.
logistics/Driver.verifiedNote: JTE, Nov 2026. Below this gross it is genuinely hard to attract drivers.

logistics/Driver.benefitNote: Drivers can usually take the vehicle home, which is worth real money to them and is often what wins the hire.

basic.label: basic monthly
basic.note: Basic monthly salary, before bonus, AWS, overtime and allowances.

gross.label: gross monthly
gross.note: Gross monthly package, basic plus overtime, incentives and allowances. For some roles the basic on its own is not what someone takes home, and not what they compare.
